synthesis: The boundary-sign proof for ζ′/ζ turns functional-equation pairing into agreement between ζ and ζ′ zero counts in the left half of the critical strip, while the separate negative-half-plane argument classifies the unavoidable ζ′ zeros there as real zeros interlacing the trivial ζ zeros. Together these results upgrade the strip criterion to the source's strengthened formulation: RH is equivalent to ζ′ having no nonreal zeros with real part below one-half.
source_support: Unit u02 establishes negativity of Re(ζ′/ζ) on the left and indented critical-line boundaries and uses argument variation to compare ζ and ζ′ zero counts; unit u03 combines Rolle's theorem with a rectangle count to prove exactly one real ζ′ zero in each stated negative interval and no other ζ′ zeros for Re(s)<0. Unit u01 states both the count theorem and the resulting Speiser criterion.
nonparaphrase_operation: Functional-equation symmetry is compressed into a boundary sign, the argument principle converts that sign into an interior count comparison, and real interlacing plus a global completeness count removes the negative real zeros from the nonreal obstruction.
limits: The count agreement is asymptotic up to O(log T), with exact agreement only along the qualified sequence in the source, and it is not a pointwise pairing of zeros. OCR corrupts one-half symbols, interval endpoints, summands, and constants, so exact formulas and indexing require the scan.
quality_reason: The synthesis requires u02's critical-strip sign-to-count mechanism and u03's independent classification of the negative half-plane; neither alone yields the strengthened nonreal-zero formulation. It preserves the distinction between aggregate counting, real-zero classification, and zero exclusion.

synthesis: Littlewood's lemma first turns the normalized kth derivative's boundary growth into both a weighted horizontal zero sum and an unweighted zero count. Subtracting the count removes total mass and isolates signed displacement from the critical line, while a separate critical-line mean bound controls total displacement strongly enough to convert the same boundary statistic into two-sided clustering, including the stated short-interval regime.
source_support: Unit u05 normalizes ζ^(k), controls the rectangle boundaries, uses differentiated functional-equation asymptotics on the left boundary, and derives weighted and unweighted zero formulas. Unit u07 subtracts one-half of the count formula from the weighted formula and differences heights to obtain the signed displacement identity. Unit u06 bounds the critical-line log-modulus integral, applies Littlewood's lemma to total horizontal displacement, and converts the resulting first-moment bounds into fixed-distance tail counts and a short-interval analogue.
nonparaphrase_operation: A boundary log-modulus integral is used as a positional moment; algebraic subtraction cancels zero mass to retain horizontal bias, and first-moment tail inequalities turn bounded displacement into concentration.
limits: These are aggregate asymptotic statements, not localization of each zero; the signed moment alone can hide left-right cancellation. The short-interval conclusion has a lower length restriction, and OCR damage makes exact constants, powers, logarithmic-integral terms, and ranges scan-dependent.
quality_reason: The signed identity needs u05's weighted and total observables together with u07's cancellation step, whereas clustering additionally needs u06's independent critical-line mean estimate. The combined mechanism therefore supplies both bias and concentration information that no one parent provides alone.

synthesis: The functional equation introduces an auxiliary J whose reflected zeros represent large-height ζ′ zeros, and the quotient J/ζ makes left-derivative and right-ζ zero displacement comparable by Littlewood's lemma. Boxes around right-side ζ zeros then localize the only possible failures of the favorable real-part sign; joining overlapping boxes into bounded chains permits local rectangle counts, and replacing the chain boundary estimate by a second-moment bound sharpens the comparison enough to obtain the moving-boundary density corollary.
source_support: Unit u08 defines J, identifies ζ′ zeros with reflected J zeros at large height, and applies Littlewood's lemma to J/ζ for an aggregate one-sided comparison. Unit u10 derives sign control away from boxes around right-side ζ zeros, uses a density estimate to terminate chains, and applies Littlewood rectangles around those chains to compare far-left ζ′ displacement with far-right ζ displacement plus an error. Unit u11 changes the left-side boundary estimate to a second-moment estimate and derives the logarithmically weighted comparison and shrinking-offset corollary.
nonparaphrase_operation: Reflection aligns the two zero populations, quotienting removes their shared analytic background, and a planar box-chain decomposition converts localized sign failures into contour regions whose boundary norms control cross-line displacement.
limits: The results compare weighted populations and do not pair individual ζ and ζ′ zeros or exclude every left ζ′ zero. They depend on density input, scale and endpoint choices, and large-height restrictions; severe OCR damage makes J identities, weights, exponents, and the moving boundary unsafe without scan verification.
quality_reason: The cross-line transfer requires u08's reflection/quotient bridge, u10's exceptional-set geometry and localized contour accounting, and u11's norm refinement. Their combination is a concrete representation change and refinement, not a generic shared theme.

synthesis: The first-derivative argument and the higher-derivative inheritance argument share a precise sign-control strategy but realize it differently: functional-equation pairing makes Re(ζ′/ζ) negative on selected boundaries for contour counting, whereas a partial-fraction expansion of ζ^(m+1)/ζ^(m) separates zero populations so finitely many left nonreal exceptions stay bounded and the infinite regularly spaced real-zero tail forces eventual negativity. The latter converts the earlier boundary-sign idea into an inductive nonvanishing mechanism for subsequent derivatives.
source_support: Unit u02 obtains negative real part of ζ′/ζ from paired ζ zeros and gamma-factor estimates and uses it with an indented contour to compare zero counts. Unit u12 expands ζ^(m+1)/ζ^(m) over real and nonreal zeros, bounds the finitely many exceptional left terms, extracts a growing negative contribution from the real-zero tail, and concludes eventual nonvanishing to the left of one-half before iterating the argument.
nonparaphrase_operation: The common bridge is negativity of a logarithmic derivative; the representation changes from functional-equation-paired pole terms supporting winding counts to a population-split partial fraction whose divergent real-zero contribution dominates finite exceptions and supports induction.
limits: The inheritance theorem assumes the preceding derivative has only finitely many nonreal zeros left of one-half and preserves finiteness rather than proving complete zero-freeness. Unit u02 alone does not establish the full base premise in the negative half-plane, so no unconditional RH-to-all-derivatives implication is inferred from these two parents alone. OCR damage affects superscripts, sums, constants, and exact boundary formulas.
quality_reason: This is a source-specific methodological generalization across u02 and u12: the same logarithmic-derivative sign observable changes both its decomposition and its consequence, from contour count equality to inductive nonvanishing. The synthesis explicitly withholds the extra base-case dependency and therefore does not turn the analogy into an unsupported causal claim.
